## How to Prompt (Copy-Paste Templates)

Use this structure: **Subject + Action + Camera + Motion + Style + Constraints**. Then add one “avoid” line to prevent common artifacts.

```text
Template 1 (UGC hook): [subject] says [claim] on handheld phone video, natural lighting, imperfect framing, fast cuts, captions on screen, avoid over-polished cinematic look.
```

```text
Template 2 (Product demo): close-up product on clean background, slow push-in camera, soft daylight, hands interacting naturally, focus on product readability, avoid jittery motion.
```

```text
Template 3 (Cinematic b-roll): wide establishing shot, smooth dolly movement, subtle parallax, realistic physics, consistent style, avoid flicker and inconsistent textures.
```

## FAQ + Final Verdict

### What is the best AI video prompt tool?

Start with Alici AI if you want an end-to-end workflow from prompt to output and iteration. Add PromptKit when you need many template starting points quickly. Use SceneSmith if you plan multi-shot sequences where continuity matters.

### Do prompt templates actually help?

Yes, because templates reduce ambiguity and help you iterate systematically. They also make it easier to compare results across tools by keeping constraints consistent. The key is to refine templates for your exact use case instead of copying blindly.

### How do I write prompts that control camera movement?

Name the shot type and camera movement explicitly, then specify the speed and direction. Add one line of motion constraints to avoid jitter or sudden cuts. Finally, keep style constraints stable while you test camera behavior.

### What should I avoid in prompts?

Avoid vague words like “beautiful” without constraints, and avoid mixing multiple styles in one prompt. Don’t leave the camera unspecified if you care about motion. Avoid adding too many details that conflict, because models often drop constraints.

### Is free tier enough to learn prompting?

Usually yes for learning structure and testing one baseline template. Free tiers often have limits that make serious production hard, but that’s fine for practice. Once you have a template that works, upgrade to iterate faster.

### How do I scale prompt variations safely?

Batch variants only after you validate one base template. Keep one variable per iteration (angle, camera, or style) so you can learn what changed results. Use a QA checklist to catch ambiguity before you generate.
